title: Tracing Actual Causes with Counterfactual Witness Maps
claim: A worked example's causal graph is turned into a finite lattice of intervention sets, which isolates the actual causes.
layout: 2 panels, DAG left, lattice center, set equations right, highlighted nodes
description: Panel (a) shows a small causal DAG for the Billy and Suzy rock-throwing example. Two dashed exogenous nodes, U_ST and U_BT, feed into ST and BT. SH and BH depend on ST and BT, and both feed into BS. True variables have double borders. BH is shaded pink and BS is shaded gray. Structural equations sit beside each node. Panel (b) shows the witness map, a layered lattice of rounded boxes of intervention sets. BS is at the bottom, and arrows lead up through the pairs {SH,BH}, {ST,BH}, {SH,BT} and {ST,BT} to the singletons ST, BT, SH and BH. Double-bordered boxes mark global targets, and pink boxes mark sets that allow a non-empty contingency. To the right, four lines of set-product equations list the witness targets, with BH in red. The eye goes first to the pink nodes in the lattice.
caption: (a) The DAG of the Billy and Suzy example. The actual world is (ST, BT, ¬BH, SH, BS) with environment (UST , UBT ) (True variables are double-bordered). (b) The witness map (Definition 6) for the counterfactual target ¬BS with double-bordered intervention sets for global targets (Definition 3) allowing the observed environment. As no singleton passes and none of these sets contains another, all four are but-for causes. The nodes that allow for non-empty contingency (¬BH) are highlighted in red. Thus we have two actual causes ST(=1) and SH(=1). See Example 3 for details. (Best viewed in color.)
abstract: Halpernian actual causation, the formal study of which events in a specific situation caused a specific outcome in acyclic structural causal models, underpins legal responsibility, moral blame, and the assessment of causal harm. Despite the rich logical framework, no prior sound and complete enumeration procedure is known for finding all actual causes in a given setting, blocking downstream tasks such as responsibility attribution, blame assessment, and causal-harm grading that aggregate over the full cause set. We close this gap by introducing witness targets: sets of joint configurations containing every counterfactual witness. In combination with an ancestor intervention grammar we derive a finite directed acyclic witness map. We prove that for every actual cause there exists a contingency set such that the joint intervention set appears as a node of this map, and present an algorithm for Tracing Actual Causes (TrAC) that is sound and complete for enumerating all actual causes of any target event. We compare TrAC empirically with existing single-cause baselines on random Boolean structural causal models, demonstrating practical feasibility for graphs of up to 15 nodes.
